manifest.help_text: Run manifest: a TSV with a header row and one data row per species. Columns: species (used as the output folder name), metadata (path to a .tsv/.csv), assemblies (path to a directory or a .txt list), target_groups (optional, comma-separated lineage labels). When unset, use the single-species --metadata / --assembly_input / --target_groups params instead.

metadata.help_text: Single-species only (--manifest unset): metadata table (.tsv/.csv) for the species. Must contain the --sample_col and --group_label columns.

assembly_input.help_text: Single-species only (--manifest unset): a directory of assembly FASTAs, or a .txt file listing one assembly path per line. Which kind it is is detected automatically.

target_groups.help_text: Single-species only (--manifest unset): comma-separated lineage labels (e.g. GPSC1,GPSC2) to run lineage-specificity candidate filtering (step 07) for, alongside the species-wide index. Unset = species-wide only.

monochrome_logs.help_text: Should logs appear in plain ASCII

primer_post_processing.help_text: Filter and soft-mask G (final candidate markers) for PCR/primer-design suitability. Off by default -- the pipeline stops at the checked candidate_markers SBWT index/FASTA unless this is turned on.

primer_min_length.help_text: Minimum candidate marker length in bp.

primer_gc_min.help_text: Minimum global GC%% a candidate marker's whole sequence must fall within.

primer_gc_max.help_text: Maximum global GC%% a candidate marker's whole sequence must fall within.

primer_window_size.help_text: Local sliding-window size (bp) for the non-designable-region GC check. Windows outside primer_gc_min-primer_gc_max are soft-masked (lowercased) in the output FASTA, not rejected -- primer3 runs with PRIMER_LOWERCASE_MASKING=1 so a primer's 3' end can't sit on a masked base but the rest of the candidate stays usable. Defaults to color_index_kmer_size (k-mer resolution).

primer_write_rejected.help_text: Write rejected (too-short / global-GC-out-of-range) candidates to their own FASTA.
